_meta.description: The physics and perception of color. Light has wavelength, but color is what brains make of it. Explore RGB, HSV, and the gap between objective light and subjective experience.

beats.concept: A salon for digital fingers. The nail color controller offers precise hue selection while color balls scatter like polish bottles on a shelf. Choose a color, apply it to the hand model, watch pigment become identity.

The grid becomes a canvas. Each cell awaits its color assignment, a pixel in a larger pattern you construct. The gridcolorizer transforms the floor into a palette - systematic, addressable, yours to paint.
Walk through light itself. Rainbow emitters line the corridor, cycling through the spectrum in slow waves. Red fades to orange fades to yellow - the continuous gradient made temporal.
Pillars of color rise along the runway, each a collection point for chromatic data. Grab the color sticks, watch the flashlight demo reveal how light creates color from darkness.
Paint meets physics. The ball painting demo turns spheres into canvases, color into gesture. Throw paint, watch it splash, see how color accumulates on curved surfaces.
The hallway dissolves into rainbow. Color transitions seamlessly from hue to hue, boundary to boundary, without the discrete steps of individual emitters.
Light reveals color by adding wavelengths. The flashlight illuminates, and surfaces respond differently — some absorb, some reflect, some fluoresce. In darkness, color vanishes.
